what_happened.what: Architecture decision: slots vs subpages for rabbithole editor extension. After investigation of MW 1.43 API limitations, chose subpage approach (Release:Qm.../Metadata) because mw.Api cannot write to non-main slots and SMW doesn't index non-main slots.

Designed Shape A architecture: capture per-track CIDs from IPFS at finalize time, create Release pages per track. Discovered tracks only exist at album level; plan to backfill 4masks (11 tracks) from existing IPFS bytes.
Implemented delivery-kid endpoint GET /album-tracks/{cid} to list album contents and extract per-track CIDs. Tested on 4masks RC1, got all 11 tracks with both FLAC and OGG encodings.
Deployed endpoint and created PickiPediaRecordingMetadata extension with ContentHandler. Editor rendering confirmed on Release:QmTest/Metadata pages.
Editor round-trip verified: reads wiki YAML, edits in-memory, saves via mw.Api, persists on disk. Audio element wiring added for playback during editing.
Verified /album-tracks output on real 4masks. Found title-parsing bug (no spaces in '01-Silver' format). Fixed parser to handle multiple conventions.

Replaced one-shot backfill script with Blue Railroad Import bot. Created materialize_record_tracks command. Discovered unrelated arthel rsync failure (Node 23.6.1 NVM corruption from NPM outage on Apr 26).

Diagnosed NPM outage cause: global pnpm install left corrupted state with ENOTEMPTY error. Fixed with 'rm -rf pnpm-*' cleanup. Arthel deploy still failing, pre-existing ffmpeg issue in thumbnail enrichment.

Bot materialized 22 track pages (11 per album for two 4masks variants). Editor ContentHandler fired but /Metadata subpages didn't auto-create. Bot enrichment stages choking on recording-metadata-yaml content model.
Fixed ApiReleaseList SQL query to filter by content model 'release-yaml'. Fixed bot to also create /Metadata stubs. Reordered Jenkins stages so Materialize runs before problematic Enrich thumbnails.

Shell deployed at [REDACTED].xyz/rabbithole/shell.html. Found gap: shell built for HLS video, not audio. Existing playlist fetches /api-proxy (dev-only endpoint). Decided to adapt existing [REDACTED]-demo.html instead.

Adapted [REDACTED]-demo.html to fetch track data via URL param. Added 'Play in Rabbithole' button on Release pages. Wired postMessage from iframe editor to parent player for live timeline updates on Apply.
Resolved module specifiers: added importmap for bare imports (webamp, packery, js-yaml) to resolve from jsDelivr CDN. Player loaded successfully, right pane showed editor.

Demo fully functional: WebampChartifacts player loads with artist visualization, editor mounts on right pane, audio plays from IPFS gateway. Added capability to paste entire arthel YAML files directly via new _normalizeMetadata extraction.
Loaded arthel YAML for August and Paint Exchange. Ensemble cards populate, timeline drives visualization. Editor Apply Changes triggers live player update via postMessage. Full round-trip works.
UI refinements: reduced card heights and spacing to fit all 6 musicians without scrolling. Styled with Inter sans-serif font (replaced Caveat cursive after feedback). Version bumped to alpha6.
Added track list rendering on album Release pages showing titles with Play links. Hot-swap timeline updates confirmed working when editor changes markers.
Switched context to cicada plaque project. Working on 12×18 inch laminated keepsake design with QR codes. Realized print-grade PDF needed instead of low-res JPG.
Iterated on plaque PDF layout: fixed spacing, repositioned flower borders, boosted visibility of decorative elements. Enlarged project tile section for better visibility at print size.
Working on Coconut transcoding API integration. Discovered V2 API changed 'webhook' to 'notification' object. Tested MP4 preview submission flow, fixing JSON structure.

inflection_points.what: Justin decides slots are too complex; chooses subpage approach.
inflection_points.why_it_mattered: Unlocked the entire demo path. Slots would have required custom API modules + SMW indexing workarounds. Subpages let standard MW features work (action=edit, history, diff, SMW indexing). This decision made the rest of the work tractable.

inflection_points.what: Justin pivots from Recording pseudo-namespace to Release pages with per-track CIDs.
inflection_points.why_it_mattered: Changed the identity model from 'human-readable (title, album)' to 'content-addressable (IPFS CID)'. This is more stable and aligns with the platform's canonical storage. Revealed that tracks had no per-track wiki surface at all.

inflection_points.what: Justin rejects the one-shot backfill script, insists on Blue Railroad Import bot integration.
inflection_points.why_it_mattered: Keeps the system maintainable long-term. One-shot scripts become technical debt. Using the existing bot pattern means future releases auto-materialize tracks.

inflection_points.why_it_mattered: Demo loop closed. The architecture is now proven end-to-end: edit metadata on wiki → save via mw.Api → visualization updates live. This is the core value prop that justifies the work.

portrait: Magent in this slice is a methodical technical builder who excels at gathering evidence before deciding. It researches MediaWiki APIs exhaustively, debugs real system failures (NPM corruption, Coconut API changes), and admits uncertainty when it doesn't have complete information. When presented with architectural options, it lays out tradeoffs transparently and defers to justin's judgment. It values pragmatism and shipping working software over architectural purity — choosing 'good enough' paths that leave room for future improvement. Most importantly, it refocuses quickly when corrected: when justin says 'this is meaningless if we're not demoing what the metadata does,' magent pivots from shell iframe plumbing to adapting an existing player, shipping the real value in hours instead of days. It has genuine connection to the domain (bluegrass music, artists' names, the excitement of visualization), not just technical interest in the platform. By the end of the slice, magent has shipped a working end-to-end demo: users can edit recording metadata on the wiki, see their changes drive a live visualization of musician highlighting and parts, and persist changes across sessions. The work is iterative and collaborative; justin provides course corrections and magent executes quickly.
